patch.value: Extension authors cannot consume the SDK's own flag, filter and loader contracts, so every first-party package hand-rewrites the baseline the CLI already declares

The stated architecture is that the CLI delivers baseline primitives through the SDK so any package can reuse them. For the command-authoring surface that is not yet true: the primitives exist, they are exported, and they are shaped so that no extension can use them.

Finding 1, the filter-flag baseline is unconsumable. src/sdk/cli-contracts/flag-contracts.ts exports LIST_FILTER_FLAG_CONTRACTS, the canonical 20-plus entry declaration of --status, --type, --tag, --priority, the deadline and updated and created windows, --ids, --assignee, --parent and the rest, complete with alias and cursor semantics, and it is public through the sdk/contracts subpath. api.registerCommand takes FlagDefinition, declared in src/core/extensions/extension-types.ts:759 with the fields long, short, value_name, description, required, enabled. CliFlagContract is a different shape entirely — flag, list, aliases. A repository-wide search finds no adapter in either direction. The canonical declaration is therefore visible to package authors and unusable by them.

The consequence is measurable. pm-calendar, pm-search-advanced and pm-governance-audit each hand-write their own --type, --tag, --priority, --status FlagDefinition blocks; jscpd at 12 lines / 60 tokens reports them as clones of one another (pm-calendar/index.ts:71 against pm-search-advanced/index.ts:164 and against pm-governance-audit/index.ts:129). They have already drifted: pm-search-advanced carries hand-added snake_case aliases such as --phrase_exact that no other package has, because there is nothing to inherit alias policy from. Every future filter flag the CLI adds has to be re-typed into each package or the package silently falls behind the baseline.

Finding 2, the runtime loader is copied rather than provided. Ten of the fifteen first-party packages contain their own ensureRuntimeBundle / loadRuntimeBundle that reads PM_CLI_PACKAGE_ROOT, joins dist/sdk paths by hand, pathToFileURL-imports the result, and validates an allow-list of expected export names. pm-beads and pm-todos are clones of each other three times over; pm-guide-shell and pm-linked-test-adapters likewise. PM_CLI_PACKAGE_ROOT is documented as first-party-only, which is a correct boundary, but the effect is that the loader problem it solves is unsolved for everyone else and re-solved by hand ten times inside the repository. A related consequence worth stating plainly: only two of fifteen first-party packages import SDK values through the public export map, so the published subpaths are barely dogfooded by the packages best placed to dogfood them.

Finding 3, the exemplar is not a kit. packages/pm-command-kit is described in its own manifest as an exemplar for the commands capability. It demonstrates registerCommand, registerFlags and registerParser; it exports nothing an author can build on. pm-kanban references it as a model to copy, not as a dependency.

Taken together these are the difference between an SDK that documents how to write a package and an SDK that supplies what a package needs. Closing it removes duplication that already exists, prevents the divergence that has already started, and is a precondition for third-party packages matching first-party capability without reverse-engineering the repository.

Scope boundary. pm-9smp7j and pm-c5f0gh own scaffold generation quality; this is about what the scaffolded package can then import. pm-x6jf owns package and extension lifecycle promotion. pm-usfg owns the SDK-first inversion in general; this is its command-authoring slice, and it is the slice a package author meets first.

An extension can declare the standard filter-flag set by consuming an SDK export rather than by restating FlagDefinition objects, and adding a filter flag to the CLI baseline reaches consuming packages without per-package edits. The SDK provides the runtime-resolution helper that the ten first-party copies of ensureRuntimeBundle currently implement, so no package hand-joins dist paths; the first-party copies are replaced by it. Alias and cursor semantics attached to a baseline flag are inherited rather than re-declared, and pm-search-advanced's divergent aliases are either adopted into the baseline or dropped. At least one first-party package is migrated end to end as proof and its hand-written tables are deleted. A regression test asserts that a package built only against public SDK subpaths can register a command carrying the full baseline filter set.
